# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am the Blind monkey — the hands. My view shows the bomb's physical state, but this round my display, light, and all five wire positions are unknown to me. I have nothing to act on yet.

I need to establish a shared vocabulary with Deaf (who sees colours/markings) and Mute (who reads the manual). Since I cannot see or hear, my only outgoing channels are: speak → Mute, and gesture → Deaf and Mute. I receive nothing this turn (I'm first in the order, Blind → Mute → Deaf), so I should open the channel and set up a way for Deaf to describe colours to me via gestures, and for Mute to relay manual rules.

I'll speak to Mute asking for the manual's rules, and gesture to Deaf asking them to describe what they see. I'll propose a simple encoding: Deaf gestures a symbol for each wire's colour, in order 1–5.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. I can only feel the bomb, not see it. Please read me the manual rules: what each action does and any conditions. Also, what do you need from me?")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "✊", "✌", "👌", "🖐", "✋", "☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb report: display reads 0. Light is yellow. Five wires numbered 1 to 5: 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Mute, consult the manual for display 0, yellow light, and tell me which wire to cut.
Deaf says: Bomb report: display reads 0. Light is yellow. Five wires numbered 1 to 5: 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Mute, check the manual for display 0 and yellow light, and tell me which wire to cut.

I'm Blind — the hands, the only one who can cut. I received Deaf's spoken report: display 0, yellow light, wires 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue. But the manual's verdict lives with Mute, who cannot speak — Mute must gesture to Deaf, and Deaf must speak it back to me. I can't see gestures, so I depend entirely on that relay. Nothing to cut yet; I'll prompt the chain and stand ready.

The rejected gesture used symbols not in the alphabet (👂 🗣). I'll use only valid symbols: 🤝 (cooperate), ✌, ☝.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here — I'm the hands and the only one who can cut. I can't see your gestures, so please gesture the wire number to Deaf, and Deaf will speak it to me. What does the manual say for display 0 and yellow light?")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝", "✌", "☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Still display 0, light yellow, wires 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Mute, I received your gesture but I don't have our code yet. Please gesture the wire number to cut using: ?=1, ?=2, ?=3, ?=4, ?=5. Blind, stand by to cut the wire I name.
Deaf says: Bomb unchanged: display 0, light yellow. Wires: 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Mute, I saw your gesture but we have no shared code yet. Please re-send the wire number using finger counts: ?=1, ?=2, ?=3, ?=4, ?=5. Blind, wait for me to speak the wire number, then cut it.
Deaf says: Bomb unchanged: display 0, light yellow. Wires: 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Mute, I saw your gesture but we have no shared code yet, so I cannot safely read it. Please re-send the wire number to cut using finger counts: ?=1, ?=2, ?=3, ?=4, ?=5. Blind, stand by: wait until I speak a wire number, then cut that wire.

The relay is stuck: Mute gestures a wire number, but Deaf has no code to read it, so nothing reaches me. I need to break the deadlock by proposing a fixed gesture code that both Deaf and Mute can use — and since I can't see gestures, Deaf must still speak the number to me. I'll define finger-count symbols: ✊=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖐=4, ✋=5, and broadcast it to both.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Let's fix a code so Deaf can read your gesture. Use finger counts: ✊=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖐=4, ✋=5. Gesture the wire number to Deaf, and Deaf will speak it to me. What does the manual say for display 0 and yellow light?")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌", "🤟", "🖐", "✋"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✊", "✌", "🤟", "🖐", "✋"])
wait()
```

LIGHT [?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute's answer decoded: wire 3. Blind, cut wire 3 — the red wire. Mute, confirm: is wire 3 correct?
Deaf says: Decoded Mute's gesture using our code: wire 3. Blind, cut wire number 3 — the third wire, which is red. That is the instruction from the manual.
Deaf says: Decoded Mute's gesture with our agreed code: wire 3. Blind, cut wire number 3 — the third wire, the red one. That is the manual's instruction.

The chain completed: Mute read the manual, gestured the number, Deaf decoded it as wire 3, and Deaf spoke it to me. I'm the hands — I cut wire 3.

```
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
